### Alternative Names: Hunterase, GC-1111, GC 1111, GC1111
Clinical Status: Inactive

## Product Description

Hunterase® is an enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of Hunter syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis type II, MPS II). Since 2012, Hunterase® has been made available in more than ten countries worldwide. The established efficacy and safety of Hunterase® provide a unique treatment option to patients with MPS II. (Sourced from: https://www.canbridgepharma.com/en/pipeline-products/approved-products/hunterase/)

## Materials and Methods

### Study design

This phase-3 study consisted of 2 parts conducted sequentially (Figure 1). Part 1 was designed as a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled study, in which participants were randomized to receive either idursulfase or idursulfase beta for 52 weeks. The randomization, stratified by age groups (<12 years, 12-18 years, and ≥19 years), was carried out using an interactive web response system (Medidata Balance, Medidata Solutions). The primary goal of part 1 was to establish the reproducibility of the 6-MWT by comparing the results from the idursulfase group in this study with those from the historical idursulfase group in the TKT024 study.^{13}

### Idursulfase beta (parts 1 and 2) vs historical placebo

After confirming the similarity in 6-MWT results at week 53 between the part 1 idursulfase and historical idursulfase groups, the study progressed to part 2. Because the recalculated sample size (n = 16) for the idursulfase beta group based on the part 1 result was still smaller than the original estimation (n = 24), additional 12 participants were enrolled as planned (Figure 1). A total of 24 participants in the idursulfase beta group from both parts of the study were included in the main analysis populations, including intention-to-treat, safety, and PK sets. The per-protocol set comprised 17 participants, excluding 7 (consent withdrawal = 1, primary end point measured outside the allowed time window = 6). Participants enrolled in the study were all male Asians. The mean time since initial diagnosis was 7.3 years, and the mean age at the time of enrollment was 12.0 years (Table 1). ## Abstract

### Purpose

To investigate the efficacy and safety of idursulfase beta (0.5 mg/kg weekly) in the treatment of mucopolysaccharidosis II, compared with a historical placebo from a previous idursulfase trial (TKT024).

### Methods

The study comprised 2 sequential parts. In part 1, a randomized, double-blind study, idursulfase or idursulfase beta were given for 52 weeks. In the open, single-cohort part 2 study, additional participants received idursulfase beta for 52 weeks. Data from the idursulfase beta groups from parts 1 and 2 were pooled for comparisons with the historical placebo group (n = 32). The primary end point was a change in the 6-minute walk test at week 53.

### Results

Participants in the idursulfase beta groups (n = 24) were male Asians (mean age, 12.0 years). Idursulfase beta was superior to placebo in 6-minute walk test improvement (62.2 vs 7.3 m, P < .0001). Decrease in urine glycosaminoglycan excretion (−71.13% vs 21.39%, P < .0001) and reduction in the liver (−26.67% vs −0.80%, P < .0001) and spleen volumes (−26.46% vs 7.2%, P < .0001) were significant.

MPS II is progressive and multisystemic, with significant morbidity and early mortality. The clinical spectrum is divided into severe and attenuated forms according to the presence of cognitive impairment. The clinical features include coarse facial features, recurrent ear and respiratory infections, hearing loss, airway obstruction and restriction, cardiac valvular diseases, hepatosplenomegaly, skeletal abnormalities, growth restriction, joint stiffness and neurological complications.

The treatment of MPS II was palliative before the introduction of enzyme replacement therapy (ERT). However, successful clinical trials^{1, 2, 3} have led to the approval of ERT with idursulfase by the United States Food and Drug Administration in July 2006 and with idursulfase beta by the Korea Food and Drug Administration in January 2012. Therefore, these recombinant enzymes are currently available for ERT for patients with MPS II. These two enzymes have 100% identical amino acid sequences derived from the human IDS gene (NM_000202). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What IV clinical evidence is on ClinicalTrials.gov?

NCT03920540 is a completed Phase 3 study of Hunterase (idursulfase-beta, GC1111) in males aged ≥5 years with Hunter syndrome, enrolling 32 participants at Samsung Medical Center, Seoul. Dosing in that record is 0.5 mg per kg once weekly by slow intravenous infusion. The primary outcome is change in 6-minute walk test at week 53 from baseline.

Record: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03920540 (GC1111 Phase 3 Hunter syndrome). An extension safety study is NCT07344376. The 24 August commercial wire did not republish 6-MWT deltas from those trials.

## Does this equal a US FDA approval of Hunterase?

No. The 24 August notice covers CDSCO (India) and TFDA (Taiwan) only. FDA's substance file lists idursulfase beta (Hunterase) as a UNII identity; UNII assignment is not a US marketing approval. Do not confuse Hunterase with other idursulfase products registered in the United States under different brand names.
